We show that there is a unique Markov trace on the tower of Temperley--Lieb type quotients of Hecke algebras of Coxeter type $E_n$ (for all $n \geq 6$). We explain in detail how this trace may be computed easily using tom Dieck's calculus of diagrams. As applications, we show how to use the trace to show that the diagram representation is faithful, and to compute leading coefficients of certain Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials.

There is a unique Markov trace on the tower of Temperley–Lieb type quotients of Hecke algebras associated with Coxeter type \(E_n\), for all \(n \geq 6\). This trace provides a compatible family of linear functionals on these algebras, respecting the natural inclusions in the tower and satisfying the usual Markov-type properties. Its uniqueness is significant because it shows that the trace is not merely an auxiliary construction, but an intrinsic feature of the Temperley–Lieb quotients in type \(E\).

A practical advantage of this trace is that it can be computed efficiently using tom Dieck’s diagram calculus. In this diagrammatic framework, elements of the algebra are represented by diagrams, and multiplication corresponds to diagram concatenation, together with suitable reduction rules. The Markov trace then admits a transparent graphical interpretation, making explicit computations considerably simpler than working directly with algebraic generators and relations.

The trace plays an important role in establishing the faithfulness of the diagram representation. By comparing the algebraic trace with its diagrammatic counterpart, one can show that the diagram calculus captures all algebraic information in the Temperley–Lieb quotient. In particular, if an algebra element acts trivially in the diagram representation, the properties of the trace imply that the element itself must be zero. Thus, the diagram representation is faithful.

In addition, the Markov trace has applications to Kazhdan–Lusztig theory. It can be used to compute leading coefficients of certain Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials associated with the relevant Coxeter groups. These coefficients encode important representation-theoretic and combinatorial information, and the trace provides an effective method for determining them in cases connected with the Temperley–Lieb quotients of type \(E_n\).

These quotients arise as analogues of the classical Temperley–Lieb algebra, obtained from the Hecke algebra by imposing relations that eliminate the contributions of non–fully commutative elements. The main focus is the construction, computation, and uniqueness of a Markov trace on these algebras.

A central tool in the analysis is tom Dieck’s diagram calculus. This diagrammatic framework provides a concrete way to represent elements of the Temperley–Lieb type quotient and to calculate the value of the trace. By translating algebraic expressions into diagrams, one obtains an effective method for evaluating the trace on a natural basis. The diagrammatic approach also clarifies the structure of the algebra and makes it possible to handle the exceptional Coxeter types \(E_n\), where direct algebraic calculations can be complicated.

The text proves that the Markov trace satisfying the required normalization and compatibility conditions is unique. In particular, once its value is fixed on the identity element and it is required to behave appropriately with respect to multiplication by the standard generators, the trace is completely determined. This uniqueness result is important because it shows that the diagrammatically defined trace is not merely one possible construction, but the canonical trace associated with these Temperley–Lieb type quotients.

The trace is then applied to two significant problems. First, it is used to study the faithfulness of diagram representations of the algebras. The trace provides a way to detect whether nonzero algebra elements act nontrivially in the diagrammatic representation, thereby helping to establish that the representation accurately reflects the algebraic structure. Second, the trace is used to compute leading coefficients of certain Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials. These coefficients encode subtle representation-theoretic and combinatorial information, and the Markov trace offers a practical method for determining them in the cases under consideration.

Overall, the text develops a detailed theory of Markov traces for Temperley–Lieb type quotients of Hecke algebras of type \(E_n\). By combining algebraic methods with tom Dieck’s diagram calculus, it establishes existence and uniqueness of the trace, provides explicit computational tools, and demonstrates the trace’s usefulness in both representation theory and Kazhdan–Lusztig theory.

Markov, Temperley, and Lieb are names closely connected to important ideas in modern algebra, statistical mechanics, and knot theory.

The **Temperley–Lieb algebra** was introduced by H. N. V. Temperley and E. H. Lieb in the study of lattice models in statistical mechanics. It provides an algebraic framework for describing interactions in models such as the Potts model and other systems where local connections or pairings play a central role. The algebra is generated by elements that satisfy simple relations, often represented diagrammatically by non-crossing strings or arcs. This diagrammatic nature makes the Temperley–Lieb algebra especially useful in both mathematics and physics.

The name **Markov** appears in this context through **Markov traces** and **Markov moves**. A Markov trace is a special kind of trace function defined on a tower of algebras, such as braid group algebras or Temperley–Lieb algebras. It has properties that make it invariant under operations related to braid equivalence. These ideas are closely related to **Markov’s theorem**, which describes when two braids have closures representing the same knot or link.

The connection between these concepts became especially significant in knot theory with the discovery of the **Jones polynomial**. Vaughan Jones used representations of braid groups into Temperley–Lieb algebras, together with a Markov trace, to construct a new polynomial invariant of knots and links. This invariant transformed knot theory and revealed deep links between low-dimensional topology, operator algebras, and statistical mechanics.

In simple terms, the Temperley–Lieb algebra gives a way to encode diagrams and interactions algebraically, while Markov’s ideas provide the trace and equivalence principles needed to turn those algebraic structures into topological invariants. Together, they form a bridge between physical models, algebraic structures, and the study of knots.

counterfactuals.output: We construct and analyze Markov traces on Temperley--Lieb quotients of Hecke algebras associated with Coxeter graphs of type \(E_n\). Using the defining quotient by noncommuting rank-two parabolic relations, we establish existence and uniqueness properties of trace functionals compatible with the Markov property and describe their behavior on the canonical diagram basis. The trace is shown to interact naturally with diagrammatic representations of the \(E_n\) Temperley--Lieb algebras, yielding explicit computational tools for evaluating basis elements and studying semisimplicity and Gram forms. As an application, we relate trace evaluations and diagram expansions to coefficients of Kazhdan--Lusztig basis elements in the fully commutative sector, providing effective formulas for the corresponding Kazhdan--Lusztig polynomials. These results extend known constructions in classical types and highlight the role of Markov traces as a bridge between Hecke algebra quotients, diagram calculus, and Kazhdan--Lusztig theory in exceptional Coxeter type.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main results of a paper proving uniqueness of a Markov trace on Temperley--Lieb type quotients of Hecke algebras of type \(E_n\) for \(n \ge 6\).
counterfactuals.output:
The paper’s main result is that the Temperley–Lieb type quotients of the Hecke algebras of type \(E_n\), for \(n\ge 6\), admit a **unique Markov trace** compatible with the natural tower of inclusions
\[
\mathrm{TL}(E_6)\subset \mathrm{TL}(E_7)\subset \mathrm{TL}(E_8)\subset \cdots .
\]

In broad terms, the results are:

1. **Construction of the \(E_n\) Temperley–Lieb quotients.**  
   Starting from the Hecke algebra \(H(E_n)\), the paper considers the generalized Temperley–Lieb quotient obtained by killing the usual rank-two braid-symmetrizer relations. These quotients are denoted \(\mathrm{TL}(E_n)\).

2. **A tower structure.**  
   The algebras \(\mathrm{TL}(E_n)\) form a nested sequence under the natural inclusions of Coxeter diagrams
   \[
   E_n\hookrightarrow E_{n+1}.
   \]
   This makes it meaningful to ask for a Markov trace on the whole tower.

3. **Normal-form/basis results.**  
   A key technical ingredient is a description of elements of \(\mathrm{TL}(E_n)\) in terms of suitable normal forms, often related to fully commutative elements of the Coxeter group of type \(E_n\). These normal forms allow one to reduce trace calculations recursively from \(\mathrm{TL}(E_{n+1})\) to \(\mathrm{TL}(E_n)\).

4. **Definition of Markov trace conditions.**  
   A Markov trace is a family of linear maps
   \[
   \operatorname{tr}_n:\mathrm{TL}(E_n)\to R
   \]
   satisfying:
   - normalization, usually \(\operatorname{tr}_n(1)=1\);
   - cyclicity, \(\operatorname{tr}_n(xy)=\operatorname{tr}_n(yx)\);
   - compatibility with inclusions \(\operatorname{tr}_{n+1}|_{\mathrm{TL}(E_n)}=\operatorname{tr}_n\);
   - a Markov property describing the trace of an element multiplied by the last generator.

5. **Uniqueness theorem.**  
   The central theorem proves that any family of traces satisfying the above Markov conditions is forced to take prescribed values on the normal-form basis. Hence there is **at most one** Markov trace on the tower of type \(E_n\) Temperley–Lieb quotients.

6. **Existence and recursive determination.**  
   The trace is not merely unique abstractly: the paper shows how it is determined recursively. Once the normalization and Markov parameter are fixed, the trace of every basis element in every \(\mathrm{TL}(E_n)\) is forced.

7. **Analogy with the Ocneanu/Jones trace.**  
   The result is an \(E\)-type analogue of the classical uniqueness of the Markov trace on type \(A\) Hecke algebras and their Temperley–Lieb quotients. It shows that the exceptional-type tower behaves, from the trace-theoretic point of view, much like the familiar type \(A\) Temperley–Lieb tower.

In short: the paper proves that the Temperley–Lieb quotients of Hecke algebras of type \(E_n\), \(n\ge 6\), carry a well-defined Markov trace on their natural tower, and that this trace is uniquely determined by the standard Markov trace axioms.

For each \(n\), the Temperley--Lieb algebra \(TL(E_n)\) is obtained as the quotient of the Hecke algebra by the ideal generated by the rank-two parabolic relations corresponding to noncommuting generators.  We describe these quotients uniformly along the natural tower
\[
TL(E_6)\subset TL(E_7)\subset TL(E_8)\subset \cdots,

satisfying cyclicity, compatibility with the inclusions \(TL(E_n)\hookrightarrow TL(E_{n+1})\), and the Markov property with respect to the last Temperley--Lieb generator.  The trace is determined recursively from these axioms and agrees with the canonical trace on the lower-rank algebras.
